source.title: Don't Use Large Mini-Batches, Use Local SGD
source.authors: Tao Lin; Sebastian U. Stich; Kumar Kshitij Patel; Martin Jaggi

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares standard mini-batch SGD with local and post-local SGD on natural-label classification tasks, measuring train and test performance. Its intervention differs from the original claim versions, but its results directly test large-batch conditions and measured properties associated with generalization.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the reported training/test accuracy comparisons and Hessian sharpness results. Related-work results cited from other studies are not rows. Several plotted comparisons have no extractable numerical values and are omitted where the text provides no explicit outcome.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out performance across batch sizes under equal sample-access budgets and tests whether post-local SGD reduces the large-batch penalty. These results test V5. Hessian curvature alone does not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: post-local SGD improves large-batch generalization, can match small-batch performance, and reaches flatter minima in their experiments. Their conclusion attributes part of the improvement to flatness, but the measurements provide association rather than a causal demonstration. Matching small-batch performance is not universal across the reported settings.
record.recipe_differences: The study changes the training procedure through local updates and delayed switching to post-local SGD; it does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, or the original claim's interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies with effective batch size, number of workers, local-step count, switching time, architecture, dataset, and the use of post-local versus ordinary mini-batch training. Authors report that larger H/K can cause optimization difficulties; longer epochs alleviate some optimization difficulty but do not close the reported large-batch gap in the described CIFAR-100 experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-local SGD produces lower Hessian eigenvalues than ordinary large-batch SGD in selected ResNet-20/CIFAR-10 comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-local updates can lead to lower-curvature solutions than synchronized large-batch SGD; this does not establish the specified magnitude-aware sharpness–gap relationship.

record.problems: The main CIFAR accuracy tables average three runs. Some supplementary comparisons are figure-only and provide no exact values in the text. Hessian sharpness is reported for a narrow model and dataset setting, and does not use the magnitude-aware perturbation measure specified by V7.
record.rows_left_out: Plotted accuracy sweeps in Figures 2, 3, 7-12 and some additional tables are not separately represented where the supplied text does not give assignable numerical values or explicit per-setting outcome statements. Text-described principal comparisons and Hessian measurements are retained.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning; adding post-local updates to LARS does not supply this comparison.
A comprehensive workload-dependent threshold map and isolated normalization or regularization interventions. Longer training is tested only over the reported CIFAR-100 budgets.
Dropout ablations; the language model uses fixed dropout.

The specified magnitude-aware sharpness measure, its association with measured train–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Filter-normalized landscape plots and raw Hessian spectra do not establish this compound claim.
Removal of memorized training examples and retraining.

missing.what: Record the batch-4096 CIFAR-100 comparisons and incomplete recovery: small/large/post-local H=8/H=16 accuracies are 68.84/67.34/68.38/68.30 for ResNet, 74.85/73.00/74.50/74.96 for DenseNet, and 79.78/77.82/79.53/79.80 for WideResNet, with the table's uncertainties.

Record the longer-training intervention: at 400 epochs small/large/post-local H=8/H=16 achieve 69.07/67.55/69.06/69.05; at 500 epochs they achieve 69.03/67.42/69.02/68.87. Ordinary large-batch training retains its deficit.
Record WikiText-2 validation perplexity at 120 epochs: small batch 86.50±0.35, large batch 86.90±0.49, post-local H=8 86.61±0.30 and H=16 86.85±0.13; K=16, Bloc=64, global batch 1024.

Record failure of tuned isotropic noise to improve large-batch accuracy: 92.46±0.27 versus 92.48±0.17 on CIFAR-10 and 67.15±0.26 versus 67.38±0.34 on CIFAR-100. Preserve the source's inconsistencies with Tables 11–12 rather than silently reconciling them.
Add the batch-16384 ordinary-SGD result of 76.3% and the 2048-to-16384 scheduled-batch result of 92.0%, needed to distinguish batch growth from post-local updates.

record.verdict_notes: Only V5 receives verdicts. Post-local accuracy rows bear on its recipe-adaptation clause; their states describe recovery, while ordinary-SGD rows describe the large-batch penalty. Reported ± values describe run variability, not demonstrated significance. The generic reference to omitted additional tables does not adequately disclose the substantive results in Tables 11–14.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and comparison with natural-label generalization are not tested.
No network-width sweep beyond interpolation is reported.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison is reported.
No adaptive optimizer comparison is reported; SGD with momentum and LARS are used.
The study does not map a general workload-dependent batch-size threshold or compare language-model results across large and small batches in the main reported results.
The study compares Hessian spectrum and loss-landscape sharpness for selected methods, not magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
No memorized-example removal or retraining is reported.
